meaning: The number 28,000 appears in the Bible as part of the count of fighting men from the tribe of Dan who joined David.
description: In 1 Chronicles 12:36, twenty-eight thousand six hundred fighting men from the tribe of Dan are mentioned, where 28000 forms the base number. The context is the great gathering of warriors from all the tribes of Israel who came to David in Hebron to transfer the kingdom from Saul's house to him, in accordance with the Lord's word. Each tribe contributed its forces, and the count underscores the broad support for David's kingship as an expression of God's will and national unity. The number reflects the military strength of the tribe of Dan and their participation in this historical event. As a large, concrete figure in a historical census, 28000 carries no strong independent symbolic meaning in biblical numerology, but serves as testimony to the organized and extensive support David received.

versions.meaning: The number 28,000 appears in the Bible primarily as a count of Levites appointed for service in the house of the Lord under King David.
versions.description: In 1 Chronicles 23:3-4, the Levites are counted from thirty years and upward to 38,000, of whom 24,000 were appointed to oversee the work in the Lord's house, while 28,000 are not directly mentioned as a separate group there, but the number may be linked to various counts of Levites and servants. Symbolically, large numbers associated with the Levites represent God’s order for holy service, organization, and faithfulness in worship. However, the number has no strong independent symbolic meaning in Jewish numerology (gematria) or biblical symbolism beyond its context as a concrete count in historical records.
versions.reason: [critical] The meaning field claims that 28000 appears as the number of Levites serving in the Lord's house under David, but this is incorrect. 28000 is not mentioned in 1 Chronicles 23:3-4 as a distinct group of Levites. The actual Bible verse where 28000 occurs is 1 Chronicles 12:36 (12:35 in some numbering), which refers to 28,600 fighting men from the tribe of Dan, of whom 28,000 is the base number.; [critical] The description field discusses 1 Chronicles 23:3-4 and the counting of the Levites, but even admits that 28,000 'is not directly mentioned as a separate group there'. The actual verse cited (1 Chronicles 12:36) concerns the tribe of Dan and their warriors, not the Levites. The entire description is built on a false premise.; [major] The description should be rewritten to reflect the actual Bible verse where 28,000 appears: 1 Chronicles 12:36, which speaks of 28,600 fighting men from the tribe of Dan who joined David in Hebron. The number 28,000 is the base figure in this count.; [minor] Footnotes are completely missing. It could be useful to add a footnote about the context in 1 Chronicles 12, which describes the warriors from the various tribes who came to David in Hebron to transfer Saul's kingdom to him.

footnotes.text: 1 Chronicles 12:24-41 lists warriors from all the tribes of Israel who came to Hebron to make David king over all Israel. The gathering represents a turning point where the entire nation united under one God-appointed king.

The tribe of Dan was one of the less prominent tribes in many biblical accounts, but their contribution of 28,600 men shows that they also recognized David's kingdom and provided a significant military force.
